html:
Really nail this shit down, in world modeling terms. This is pure gold for specifying the curriculum in terms of training data and a sequence of *broad* cognitive refactors, each of which takes previous models as inputs.

Why are these useful?

they specify what kinds of representations become learnable at different stages, under what environmental scaffolding, and through what kinds of experience statistics

Take Fischer’s Dynamic Skill Theory as a concrete example. It doesn’t just say "children get smarter"; it formalizes cognition as hierarchically composed skills that emerge through cycles of construction, coordination, and stabilization under task pressure

Theories of development: In dialog with Jean Piaget

Jean-Jacques Rousseau wrote Emile, or On Education in 1762. He discusses childhood development as happening in three stages. In the first stage, up to age 12, the child is guided by their emotions and impulses. In the second stage, ages 12-16, the child’s reason starts to develop. In the third and final stage, age 16 and up, the child develops into an adult.
